title: Initial, medial, final sounds
examples: Teacher, where do I hear the sound in the word cat?
How can I tell if a sound is at the beginning or the end?
Can you show me a word that has a sound in the middle?

explain.say: Listen to me say the word sun. Say it with me. Now, listen closely to the very first sound you hear. It sounds like /s/. Say /s/.
Now I will say the word cup. Say cup. What is the very last sound you hear? It sounds like /p/. Say /p/.
Next, I say the word pig. Say pig. Listen to the sound right in the middle. It sounds like /i/. Say /i/.
We can sort sounds now. I say the word mat. Does it start with /m/ or /t/? Listen again. It starts with /m/.
A common mistake is thinking the whole word is just one sound. Remember that words are made up of many small sounds. We must listen for the specific beginning, middle, or end sound.

faq.q: How do I know if a sound is at the beginning?
faq.a: The beginning sound is the first sound you hear when you say the whole word. You can pretend to tap your finger on the first syllable. You might also ask, 'What sound starts the word?'

faq.q: What is the sound in the middle of a word?
faq.a: The middle sound is the sound you hear right in the middle when you say the word slowly. It is the sound that is not at the start or the end. You could also ask, 'What sound is in the middle?'
asks: What sound is in the middle?
Can you find the middle sound?

faq.q: How do I know if a sound is at the end?
faq.a: The ending sound is the very last sound you hear when you say the word. It is the sound that finishes the word. You might ask, 'What sound ends the word?'

faq.q: Do all words have three sounds?
faq.a: No, words can have different numbers of sounds. Some words have two sounds, and some have more than three. We just listen carefully to count them.
asks: Do all words have three sounds?
How many sounds are in a word?

faq.q: Is it hard to tell the difference between sounds?
faq.a: It takes practice to listen for every little sound. Keep listening to words all the time. The more you listen, the easier it will become.
asks: How do I get better at this?

facts: Every word is made up of small sounds called phonemes.
The first sound is the beginning sound of the word.
The last sound is the ending sound of the word.
We listen with our whole ears to find these sounds.

quiz.say: The word 'dog' starts with the sound /d/. What is the sound?
quiz.why: The sound /d/ is the first sound you hear when you say dog.

wrong.0: This is the ending sound, but the question asks for the start.
wrong.1: You must only pick one sound for the start.
wrong.3: This is the middle sound, but the question asks for the start.

quiz.say: The word 'cup' ends with the sound /p/. What is the sound?
quiz.why: The sound /p/ is the very last sound you hear when you say cup.

wrong.0: This is the beginning sound, but the question asks for the end.
wrong.1: This is the middle sound, but the question asks for the end.
wrong.2: You must only pick one sound for the end.

quiz.say: In the word 'pig', the sound in the middle is /ɪ/. What is the sound?
quiz.why: The sound /ɪ/ is the sound you hear right in the middle of the word pig.

wrong.0: This is the beginning sound, but the question asks for the middle.
wrong.1: This is the ending sound, but the question asks for the middle.
wrong.2: You must only pick one sound for the middle.
